office.title: Indiana State Senator
office.summary: Members of the Indiana Senate write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The Senate has 50 members, each representing one district for a four-year term; about half the seats are elected every two years [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 25 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year, under Article 4 of the Indiana Constitution [1].

incumbent.name: Kyle Walker
incumbent.summary: Sen. Kyle Walker (R-Lawrence), who has held the seat since 2020 and won reelection in 2022 with 55% of the vote, announced in December 2025 that he would not seek reelection and would finish his term through the November 2026 election [3, 4]. He described the decision as a new chapter in his professional career [3].
record: November 2025: Announced opposition to the proposed mid-decade congressional redistricting, citing constituent feedback: "With 93 percent opposed, and as their voice in the Indiana Senate, I'll be voting no" [3]. The Senate rejected the plan 31–19 on Dec. 11, 2025 [5].

December 3, 2025: Said he would not seek reelection; his statement did not mention redistricting, according to the Indiana Capital Chronicle, which reported he had resigned as executive vice president of MO Strategies, a consulting firm led by the chair of a pro-redistricting nonprofit [3].

In his announcement, Walker cited changing the local income tax distribution formula so Fishers receives a more equitable share, and creating a Sports and Tourism Bid Fund to help communities host major events [3].

race_context: Senate District 31 includes parts of Hamilton, Hancock and Marion counties, more than 135,000 residents, according to WRTV [6]; WFYI describes it as Fishers, parts of northern Lawrence Township and the Geist Reservoir area [4].

It is an open seat: Republican Sen. Kyle Walker is not running again [3]. The Indiana Capital Chronicle called it one of the state's few politically competitive Senate districts; Walker won 55% in 2022 [3, 4].

May 5, 2026 Republican primary: Juanita Albright 3,516 votes (37.7%), Tiffanie Ditlevson 2,332 (25.0%), Travis Hankins 1,781 (19.1%), Jan Kepley Keefer 1,699 (18.2%), according to Wikipedia's compilation of results [7].
May 5, 2026 Democratic primary: Kerry Forestal 4,153 votes (37.7%), Catherine Torzewski 3,909 (35.5%), Lasima Packett 1,805 (16.4%), Andrew Dezelan 1,141 (10.4%) [7].
No general-election debate or forum between Albright and Forestal was found in reviewed coverage.

Both nominees list cost of living, health care costs and public safety among their priorities; Albright's materials emphasize tax cuts and property tax relief, while Forestal's emphasize utility, health care and grocery costs [8, 4, 9].

candidates.summary: Albright is a Fishers physician and president of the Hamilton Southeastern (HSE) School Board who won a four-way Republican primary [10, 7].
background: Has practiced medicine and lived in Fishers for more than 20 years [10].

Elected to the Hamilton Southeastern School Board and serves as its president; her campaign says the district reached its highest graduation rate during her term and that she has overseen a budget of more than $340 million [8, 10].
Appointed by Fishers Mayor Scott Fadness to the Fishers Senior Center Committee [10].
path_to_ballot: Filed Jan. 7, 2026 [10]; won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 37.7% over Tiffanie Ditlevson, Travis Hankins and Jan Kepley Keefer, per Wikipedia's compilation [7].

items: Her campaign site says she will work to lower property taxes in the district and help seniors stay in their homes [8].
Says Hoosiers need "relief, not more government-driven costs" and supports tax cuts, balanced budgets and making housing, groceries and health care more affordable [8].
Supports "practical, market-based reforms" to lower premiums and out-of-pocket costs, including prescription drugs, with emphasis on care for older Hoosiers [8, 10].
Supports adequate funding for local schools, teacher support, parental involvement, high academic standards and local decision-making [8].
Supports keeping violent offenders incarcerated and mental health treatment for low-risk, nonviolent offenders to reduce reoffending [8].

on_incumbent: No statements by Albright about Sen. Walker's record or the seat's direction were found beyond her own platform. She told WFYI, "I bring vast experience in healthcare and education, which are two of the largest issues facing Hoosiers" [4].
plans: Running on lowering inflation and the cost of living, fiscal responsibility, quality education and public safety [10].
endorsements_finance: Her campaign lists Americans for Prosperity–Indiana, Hoosiers for Quality Education, the Indiana Chamber of Commerce and the Indiana State Police Alliance [8]; she also told WFYI she had Indiana Right to Life's endorsement [4].
No fundraising totals were found in reviewed coverage.
gaps: Search snippets report Albright took about 41% of the Republican vote in Hamilton County and 26% in Marion County (Current Publishing); unverified.
Search snippets report an Indiana Family Action PAC endorsement and an endorsement from Gov. Mike Braun; unverified.

Current Publishing articles (primary results, announcement) were inaccessible (403); the Indiana Capital Chronicle voter guide (which reportedly notes she did not return its survey) was also inaccessible.
No fundraising data or general-election forum found.
Votes she would cast on specific bills (e.g., property-tax or budget legislation) not stated.
A reported primary endorsement by U.S. Sen. Jim Banks was found only on a local blog and is not included.

candidates.summary: Forestal is the Democratic Marion County sheriff, in his second and final term, and a former U.S. Marshal for the Southern District of Indiana [9]. He has not served in the General Assembly.
background: Has worked in Marion County law enforcement since 1977, beginning as a patrol deputy [9, 6].
Appointed U.S. Marshal for the Southern District of Indiana by President Barack Obama in 2010 [9].
Elected Marion County sheriff in 2018 and reelected in 2022; he is term-limited and oversees a $150 million budget [6, 9].
Received the NAACP's State Rep. Bill Crawford Legacy Award in 2025 [9]. Lives in the district [6].
path_to_ballot: Announced in December 2025 [6]; won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.7% over Catherine Torzewski, Lasima Packett and Andrew Dezelan, per Wikipedia's compilation [7].

items: Lists lowering household costs — housing, utilities and health care — plus infrastructure and economic development as priorities [4].
Promised "pragmatic, values-driven leadership" on rising costs including utilities and health care [9].
Lists public safety, including mental health and addiction treatment, as a priority [4]; says he implemented evidence-based violence prevention programs as sheriff [6].

on_incumbent: No statements by Forestal about Sen. Walker's record were found. On the seat, he said constituents' "voice in the State Senate will fight every single day to make their lives better" [9].
plans: Says he will work to bring down utility and health care costs while continuing a public-safety focus [6].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising totals were found in reviewed coverage.
gaps: The Indiana Capital Chronicle reported criticism of Forestal for working with federal immigration enforcement and holding detainees in the county jail [9]; no response from Forestal was found.
He reportedly returned the Indiana Capital Chronicle voter-guide survey, but the guide was inaccessible (403).
No campaign website, endorsements or finance data located.
Not a current or former state legislator (the research note suggesting this was not borne out).
